chunks: 3215 - Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said in his will to his son Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, may Allah be pleased with him: “My son, do not say what you do not know; rather, do not say everything that you know. For Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has imposed obligations upon all your limbs, by which He will argue against you on the Day of Resurrection and ask you about them. He reminded them, admonished them, warned them, and disciplined them, and He did not leave them neglected. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:”
“And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those shall be questioned about.”
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge, and you counted it trivial while it is immense with Allah.”
Then He bound them to obedience to Him, so He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“O you who believe, bow, and prostrate, and worship your Lord, and do good, so that you may succeed.”
So this is a comprehensive obligation, mandatory upon the limbs. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“And that the places of sajdah belong to Allah, so do not call upon anyone along with Allah.”
By al-masājid, He means the face, the two hands, the two knees, and the two big toes. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“And you did not hide yourselves lest your hearing, your sights, or your skins should testify against you.”

By al-julūd, He means the private parts. Then He specified each limb from among your limbs with an obligation and stated it explicitly. So He made it obligatory upon hearing that you do not incline with it toward acts of disobedience. Thus He, Mighty and Majestic, said:

“And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being disbelieved in and mocked, then do not sit with them until they enter into another discourse; indeed, then you would be like them.”
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“And when you see those who engage in discourse concerning Our signs, then turn away from them until they engage in another discourse.”
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made an exception for the case of forgetfulness, and said:
“And if Satan causes you to forget, then after the reminder do not sit with the wrongdoing people.”
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“So give glad tidings to My servants — those who listen to the word and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the possessors of intellect.”
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“And when they pass by vain speech, they pass by with dignity.”
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“And when they hear vain speech, they turn away from it.”

So this is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made obligatory upon hearing, and this is its function. And He made it obligatory upon sight that it not look at what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden for it. So He, Exalted is He among speakers, said:
“Say to the believing men that they should lower some of their gaze and guard their private parts.”

Thus He forbade that anyone should look at the private part of another. And He made it obligatory upon the tongue acknowledgment and expression of what the heart has bound itself to. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“Say: We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to us” — the verse.
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“And speak to the people with goodness.”
And He made obligatory upon the heart — and it is the commander of the limbs, by which you reason and understand, and from whose command and judgment you proceed — so He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“Except one who is compelled while his heart is at rest in iman” — the verse.
And He, Exalted is He, said when He informed about a people who were given iman upon their mouths while their hearts had not believed. So He, Exalted is He, said:
“Those who said: We believe, with their mouths, while their hearts did not believe.”
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“Surely, by the dhikr of Allah do hearts find rest.”
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“And whether you reveal what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it; then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.”

And He made it obligatory upon the two hands that you do not extend them toward what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden to you, and that you use them in His obedience. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“O you who believe, when you rise for salat, then wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles.”
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“So when you meet those who disbelieve, then striking of the necks.”
And He made it obligatory upon the two feet that you move them in His obedience and that you not walk with them the walk of one disobedient. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“And do not walk in the earth exultantly; surely you will never tear through the earth, nor will you ever reach the mountains in height. All of that — its evil is, with your Lord, detested.”
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“Today We shall seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness regarding what they used to earn.”

So He informed about them that they will testify against their possessor on the Day of Resurrection. This is what Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made obligatory upon your limbs. So have taqwa of Allah, my son, and employ them in His obedience and His good pleasure. Beware lest Allah, Exalted is He, see you in disobedience to Him, or miss you in obedience to Him, so that you become among the losers. Hold fast to reciting the Qur’an, acting by what is in it, adhering to its obligations, its laws, its halal and its haram, its commands and its prohibitions, and keeping vigil with it and reciting it in your night and your day. For it is a covenant from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to His creation. Thus it is obligatory upon every Muslim to look each day into his covenant, even if only fifty verses. And know that the درجات of Jannah are according to the number of the verses of the Qur’an. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said to the reciter of the Qur’an: Recite and ascend. There will not be in Jannah, after the Prophets and the truthful ones, anyone higher in rank than him.”
And the will is lengthy; we have taken from it the place of need. And there is no might and no power except by Allah, the Most High, the Great, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

key_terms.فَرَائِضَ: obligatory duties imposed by Allah upon a person
key_terms.ٱلسَّمْعَ: hearing, as a faculty accountable for what it listens to
key_terms.ٱلْبَصَرِ: sight, as a faculty restricted from the forbidden
key_terms.ٱلْجَوَارِحِ: the bodily limbs and faculties that carry moral responsibility
key_terms.ٱلْقَلْبِ: the heart, the inward commander of understanding and intention
key_terms.ٱلْقُرْآنِ: the divine covenant to be recited and acted upon
key_terms.ٱلْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when the limbs will be questioned and testify

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali عليه السلام teach about the obligations of the limbs and accountability on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: This narration is a moral exhortation from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام explaining that every limb has divinely assigned obligations and will testify on the Day of Resurrection. It links ethical self-restraint, obedience, and Qur’an recitation to accountability, spiritual discipline, and elevation in Jannah.
